item.title: The Simplest Thing That Could Possibly Work
item.description:
There’s a question from Extreme Programming that I keep returning to:

What is the simplest thing that could possibly work?

It sounds almost naive. But it’s one of the most useful filters I’ve found when designing systems.

The Complexity Trap

Engineers — myself included — tend to over-engineer. We anticipate scale, future requirements, and edge cases that may never materialize. We reach for distributed systems before we’ve saturated a single machine. We add abstraction layers before we have two concrete cases to abstract.

item.title: On Writing Good Commit Messages
item.description:
A commit message is a letter to your future self. Make it worth reading.

The Problem with Bad Commits

We’ve all seen them:

fix
wip
asdf
final final FINAL

These tell you nothing. Six months later, when a bug surfaces and you’re spelunking through git log, these are useless noise.

The Rule of Thumb

The subject line of a commit should complete this sentence:

If applied, this commit will…

So: “Add input validation to login form” rather than “validation stuff”.
